Text2: Ludhiana: Nearly 100  patients  diagnosed with Hepatitis C have been waiting for treatment to start for the last few months, as the  civil hospital  is grappling with a shortage of medicines.
Officials have confirmed that the civil hospital did not have enough supply of medicines to start the treatment of new Hepatitis C patients. Therefore, only old patients are getting medicine at the hospital.
Doctors emphasise that consistent medication is vital to treating Hepatitis C, making it crucial for patients to receive timely treatment. However, with limited supplies, prioritising follow-up patients has left new cases in a state of uncertainty.
One of the reasons why new patients are also not being treated is that doctors cannot stop the treatment of follow-up patients.
As per sources, around 1,550 patients have been getting treated for Hepatitis C in the district.
Hepatitis C is an infectious disease that primarily affects the liver and is caused by various means - such as contaminated needles, blood transfusion, sexual intercourse or from an infected mother to her child. The symptoms of this disease include fever, dark urine, nausea, yellow skin, tiredness, jaundice, yellow eyes, and more.
Dr Ramanpreet Kaur, district epidemiologist, said confirmed that around 100 patients had been on hold due to shortage of medicines. "With the available stock, we can give medicines to only follow-up patients. We are continuously sending our demand to govt and will start giving medicines to new patients when we get the required supply," she said.
She added around 40 new patients had been called on Monday and their medicines would be initiated in one or two days.
In 2016, Punjab became the first state in the country to start providing free medicines to Hepatitis C patients under National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme (NVHCP). After Punjab, central govt implemented this initiative across the country under National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme.

Text1: A doctor cannot prescribe drugs regulated in Schedule X of the Drug and Cosmetic Act, for example anti-cancer drugs, morphine and codeine, if he or she is consulting via tele-medicine, the National Medical Commission ( NMC ) has said.
In its first-ever guideline for practice of telemedicine in India, which was notified recently, NMC says only drugs used for common ailments that are available 'over the counter', for example topical antibiotics, antiseptics, antacids and cough suppressants, can be prescribed via telemedicine consultation.
NMC also suggested that drugs like antifungal agents for skin ailments, antibiotic eye drops for conjunctivitis, antibiotics for abscesses, laryngitis and other conditions should be prescribed over video consultation. There is no restriction on the mode of tele-communication for consultation for prescription for 'add-on' drugs which can be used to optimise or better manage an existing condition, not a new drug for a different medical condition or disease. These drugs, the NMC guidelines for practicing telemedicine suggest, can be prescribed via video, audio or text-based consultation.
 The guidelines have been notified as a part of the National Medical Commission Registered Medical Practitioner (Professional Conduct) Regulations, 2023. 
The guidelines mandate doctors to issue an e-prescription for tele-consultation. It should contain their name, qualifications, registration number, address and contact details. of the RMP. The guidelines also mandate mentioning the name, age, sex, identification and contact details of the patient in case of tele-consultation. Other must-haves in an e-prescription include: name of the drug/s being prescribed in capital letters along with a clear mention of the formulation, dose, frequency and duration for which the drug/s is/are to be taken. 
Doctors or registered medical practitioners (RMPs) insisting on telemedicine, when the patient is willing to travel to a facility and/or requests an in-person consultation will be considered a professional misconduct, as per new norms. 
The guidelines mandate doctors to maintain a digital trail of documents such as patient records, reports, images, diagnostics, data etc for three years from the date of the last consultation with the patient. As for the fee, the new guidelines say, telemedicine consultations should be treated the same way as in-person consultations with regard to consultation charges or fee.

Text2: NEW DELHI: The sudden death of  teen actor  due to an autoimmune disorder has sparked a discussion on the need for greater awareness about such illness - both among the  public  and physicians.
The actor suffered from  dermatomyositis , an autoimmune disorder that primarily affects the skin and the skeletal muscle. Her family said the actor had been suffering from symptoms suggestive of the disease for almost two months but the diagnosis could be made only two weeks ago.

"She complained about swelling in the left hand initially.Later, she also developed skin problems for which we went to several doctors but to no avail. Two weeks ago, when we took her to AIIMS, it was confirmed that our daughter was suffering from dermatomyositis, which is an extremely rare disease. She was treated with steroids and several other medications but, unfortunately, she did not survive," the actor's father told ANI.
According to Dr Uma Kumar, professor and head of rheumatology department at AIIMS, as true for most autoimmune or auto-inflammatory rheumatic diseases, dermatomyositis also requires a high index of suspicion and caution in diagnosing as it has many mimickers. "Often such patients report to dermatologist, pulmonologist, neurologist, nephrologist etc before reaching to rheumatologist because of the multi-systemic nature of the disease," she said.
The treatment of dermatomyositis, which predominantly affects skin and muscles but can involve joints, lung, heart, kidneys, etc, includes administering anti-inflammatory medicines. In some cases, patients may also require administering immunosuppressive medicines.
"Autoimmune disorders occur when the body's immune system attacks and destroys healthy body tissue by mistake. Anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive medicines, among others, are administered to slow the process. Most patients respond well to the treatment and only about 5% have fulminant courses," the doctor said.

Though no one knows the exact cause of autoimmune disorders, research suggests it can be triggered by multiple factors, for example recurrent viral infection, smoking, air pollution, certain drugs and chronic stress. Genetic predisposition also plays a significant role, doctors say.
Dr Kameshwar Prasad, professor emeritus of neurology at AIIMS, who is currently heading the neurology division at Fortis Vasant Kunj, told TOI that people who have been PCR positive for Covid-19 have two to three times higher risk of developing autoimmune diseases, including dermatomyositis, compared to those who never tested positive for the viral infection. "The risk also depends on the severity ofCovid-19," he said.
A study published recently in eClinical Medicine, part of Lancet Discovery Science, says that prolonged inflammation in Covid-19 might trigger the immune system to create antibodies against virus antigens that share structural similarities with self-antigens and lead to a cross-reactive response against both self-antigens and non-self-antigens.

Text1: KOCHI: Three years after the trail turned cold in the sensational robbery of a centuries-old emerald idol of Lord Shiva from Sringeri Mutt in Kalady, Kerala police claim they have cracked the case. State crime branch officials said they suspect Subhash Kapoor, an UP-born US citizen and antique smuggler who runs a gallery in New York, and is the public face of a clandestine international racket in ancient artefacts.
 Kapoor is allegedly behind a number of idol heists from Tamil Nadu as well, and police here surmise that he is involved in the burglary of five idols, similar to the Sringeri one, from other temples in Kerala. A report of the economic offences wing of the Tamil Nadu police reveals that Kapoor runs a private museum called Art of the Past and an export company, Nimbus Import Inc, in New York. He specialises in shipping out and selling stolen antiques to museums, private collectors and dealers through a wide network ranging across India, Pakistan, Dubai, Hong Kong, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Cambodia and Thailand.
 Kapoor was arrested in Germany in October 2011 following a red corner notice issued by the CBI with the help of Interpol. "We will approach the TN police and are planning to make a joint effort to extradite him from Germany," a senior crime branch official, who requested anonymity, told TOI.
 Kapoor is believed to have masterminded the theft of 18 panchaloha idols from the Arulmigu Sundareswarar and Varadharaja Perumal temples at Suthamalli village in Ariyalur district on April 13, 2008. "The TN police are already at his back in connection with the theft of antique idols from various temples in Tamil Nadu. We are now expecting to make a breakthrough in the Sringeri Mutt case also," the official said.
 The TN police report points out that antique idols were shipped from Chennai harbour to US in two batches between May and July 2006. Kapoor paid a dollar equivalent of Rs 1,16,37,694 from his account with HSBC Bank in New York to an accomplice identified as Sanjivi Asokan, suspected to be his point man in Chennai. Asokan was earlier arrested by a special team of the Kerala police in connection with the Sringeri case but it is only now that they became aware of his link with Kapoor.

Text1: Noida: The agency responsible for maintenance at the  Noida Extension mall , where a falling piece of railing killed a  shop owner  and his  apprentice  on Sunday, wrote to police, saying the collapse occurred because of "strong winds".
Ajay Bisht, manager of Kanav Consultancy and Liasioning Pvt Ltd, wrote on Monday that a team was anyway inspecting the Blue Sapphire Mall premises after complaints from workers that several fittings had become weak at the base because of  strong winds  over the past couple of days.
The team, he claimed, was supposed to inspect the railing too, but it collapsed before that. "This portion appeared fine in our earlier inspections. The incident happened because of strong winds. The mall owners or management are not responsible for this," Bisht wrote.
The mall promoters - Pradeep and Sheetal Aggarwal - and officials of the maintenance agency have been booked under IPC Section 304A (causing death by negligence).
A little before Sunday noon, Harendra Bhati - who owned a shop on the first floor of the mall - and Shakeel - a painter who worked for him - died after the iron railing fell on them from the fifth floor.
On Monday, the Noida DM constituted a team under ADM (finance) to carry out a structural audit of the mall building. The fire department will also submit a report while a private agency will examine the elevators.
Police commissioner Laxmi Singh told TOI they were scanning the contract papers on maintenance of the mall. "The primary liability of the incident lies with the person in charge of the mall's maintenance. We are investigating the contract documents and are in the process of identifying the accused," she added.
A fire safety audit was also conducted by the chief fire officer on Monday. "The CFO has been asked to submit a report to me. Based on the findings, we will take action," Singh said.
DM Manish Verma said the structural audit report would be ready soon. "A team comprising a PWD engineer, and electrical and structural safety experts were sent to the mall on Monday. Text2: Noida: Five employees - among them an  assistant vice-president  and senior manager - of the private company responsible for maintaining lifts at an office building in Sector 125 were arrested for negligence on Saturday, a day after nine staffers of an IT firm suffered injuries when the elevator went on a  free fall  from the eighth floor to the basement.
The five who were arrested were identified as Mohit Pant and Abhineet Mathur - assistant community  managers  of Awfis Space Solutions - assistant vice-president Neetu Chandna Bisht, senior manager Shraddha Thapa and lift service man Ramesh Chandra.
Around 5.45pm on Friday, the nine employees of Erasmith Technologies Pvt Ltd - which deals in software development - had boarded the lift on the eighth floor when it collapsed. As it landed in the basement with a loud thud, the nine hit themselves against the walls of the lift and suffered grievous injuries and fractures. They were brought out of the lift and taken to a nearby private hospital.
The lift collapse occurred in River-Side Towerr, a building that houses the offices of several companies. Erasmith is located on the eighth floor of the tower. 
Police said the action against the  lift company  officials followed a complaint by Naveen Jangira, the CEO of Erasmith Technologies. He alleged that the elevator had malfunctioned earlier too, but no action was taken to make it safer.
"We registered an FIR at the Sector 126 police station against Awfis Space Solutions late on Friday evening. The CEO of the IT firm whose employees were injured alleged that they had raised repeated concerns about the lift's functioning, but to no avail. So, we decided to take action against the lift company's officials for negligence," said Harish Chander, DCP (Noida).
The FIR against the five officials were registered under sections 287 (negligent conduct with respect to machinery), 308 (attempt to commit culpable homicide) and 325 (voluntarily causing grievous hurt) of the IPC.
"Awfis was responsible for maintaining lifts at River-Side Towerr. Preliminary probe revealed that they were too negligent about the complaints raised against the lifts' functioning. Nothing was done to fix them," the DCP added.
Of the nine injured persons, five are undergoing treatment for fractures and other injuries in the ICU. Two were discharged from the hospital on Saturday.
With lift malfunctions on the rise, the UP government is planning to pass a legislation to make elevators safer for users. The legislation will include mandatory maintenance of elevators every year, their registration and penal action against agencies concerned in cases of negligence.
The draft of this Act has been pending with the government for several years now. Although proposals were submitted by the Noida Authority in 2015 and 2018, the Act is yet to be implemented. The Ghaziabad Development Authority also submitted a file to the government in 2018, making a similar plea.

Text1: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Even as the state government has decided to set up cancer care centres in each district and provide free treatment to all, the post graduate diploma course in radio therapy offered by the medical college hospital (MCH), Thiruvananthapuram, is yet to get its recognition from the medical council of India (MCI).
 "The two-year course is being offered at the MCH for the last ten years without MCI recognition.It failed to get the recognition as the department did not fulfill the MCI guidelines on infrastructural facilities,'' said Dr P S Sabari Nath of Kerala medical post graduate association.
 Students who complete the course find it difficult to get placed in any organization since the course is not certified. The council had sanctioned two seats for the course in 1978.
 "Facilities of the radio therapy department were handed over to the Regional Cancer Centre when it was formed. However, after that no development occurred in the therapy department at the medical college hospital,'' said Dr K Mohanan, state president of Kerala medical teacher's association.After repeated efforts for the past two years the government had sanctioned Rs 35 crore to set up the basic infrastructure facilities at the department. But, the finance ministry has now released only Rs 7.5 crore with which linear accelerator and other radiation equipment will have to be purchased, said Dr Mohanan.
 "If the remaining funds are not released immediately, the course will not get recognition. Students who are completing the course are joining MD course which would take another three years. If the course was recognized he/she should have completed the MD course in two years,'' said Dr Sabari Nath.
 It was the setting up of the Regional Cancer Centre that neglected the development of the radio therapy department at the MCH.
 Initially, MD course was sanctioned only in the MCH and the students were trained at the RCC. Now the MCI has given recognition for the MD course in the RCC also.
 Health minister V S Sivakumar has assured that the radio therapy department at the MCH would be developed soon and all necessary infrastructure facilities would be immediately made available. "The government plans to set up cancer care centres in all medical college hospitals across the state. Hence there will be a rapid progress in the facilities of the departments of the MCHs soon,'' said the minister.

Text2: I'm in a high-ceilinged studio space with whitewashed floors and bright lighting. This place doesn't look much like a nightclub and there's no party atmosphere, but I have come to dance, or at least to take part in an Introduction to Dance class: I want to find out if there is any hope for me. Actually, I don't think I'm a terrible dancer. There was a time in my 20s when I would go clubbing without fail every week and it didn't take much to lure me on to the dancefloor. Dancing gave me the opportunity to totally lose myself; for someone like me who doesn't drink or do drugs it wasn't just intensely pleasurable – it also felt necessary. Today I am a middle-aged, married, mortgaged, fortysomething father. My opportunities for dancing have diminished, as has my confidence. Tania, our instructor, takes us through our first moves. I hadn't realised until now how much of my dancing style was arm-based – random pointing played a crucial role in my technique. I also realise how little I was moving my legs and especially my upper body. It's almost as if I wasn't allowing myself to respond instinctively to the music and the beat. Tania stresses the importance of relaxing the chest. She shows us how to crumple and twist our middle section by breaking it into different areas – the upper chest, stomach and hips – and trying to move one part without affecting the others. I am even asked to do something called a ripple. It's the sort of move I imagine pole dancers learn during their training, and indeed when done well it looks as if your body is undulating in musical ecstasy. It doesn't quite look like that when I do it. Having to isolate different moves and focus on the chest, then shoulders and neck, makes me appreciate that my style of dancing is stiff rather than fluid – more Ian Curtis than Curtis Mayfield – and the way to improve that is to focus on the core rather than the limbs. Tania's promise, or warning, that the class would be funky, meant the anodyne hip hop music we were dancing to wasn't anything I would usually subject myself to and the moves that suited the music- sudden drops with legs apart, tapping the inside and outside of one's shoes as you shake your lower leg- weren't things I could imagine doing while listening to Joy Division: good dancing demands good music. I stare at myself in the huge mirrors, dancing to hip hop music – suddenly dropping down with legs apart or shaking my lower legs – and at first I feel self-conscious. It's hard not to enviously glance at the others as they morph into Michael Jackson and Beyoncé. By the end of the class I am totally exhausted and just a little bit exhilarated. The most important lesson I have learned isn't any particular dance move, although that helps, but just that it is so freeing to have an outlet to dance where for an hour and a half I am not thinking about work or family or Twitter: just about how good it is to move your body to the music. Text1: ‘We are caged in simulations," reads the gigantic, stage-wide convex screen as a legion of neon robots with trombones herald Matt Bellamy rising from the centre of the stadium with android fanfares, as if the AI have arisen and stolen the jobs of the nearest marching band. So have Muse been a glitch in the matrix all along? They always seemed a spectacular rock'n'roll programming error: three Teignmouth lads who became superstars by deciphering the malevolent sociopolitical virus code of the 21st century and delivering their findings in a blitz of operatic space rock, dystopian stage fantasies and solos resembling a cyborg Queen ferociously malfunctioning. Certainly the tour for 2015's Drones – when remote-controlled spheres strafed the stands and diaphanous screens stretched the length of arenas – was so immersive that it's surely only a matter of technology before they go fully virtual and play stadium gigs in your squat. Meantime, they bring the retro-futurist 80s teen flick unrealities of their VR-themed new album Simulation Theory to life. Donning glowing glasses throughout, Bellamy plays an avatar being hunted through the machine. Space zombies chase him along the ego ramp throughout synthrock anthem Thought Contagion. Acrobats in isolation suits walk vertically down the screen during the Arabian-inflected Break It To Me, tracking him with flashlights. A 23rd-century task force, wielding steam-throwers, invade the stage for Propaganda, the sound of Prince being crushed beneath a grooving Terminator. These breezy, synthetic new tunes interface seamlessly with Uprising, Supermassive Black Hole and Psycho – tracks that always sounded like glam being shot around the Large Hadron Collider – and the first hour zips by. A plodding gospel Dig Down hobbles the pace, but there's enough momentum to sci-fi anthems such as Mercy and pop-metal classics Hysteria, Time Is Running Out and hellfire opera Take A Bow – sung by Bellamy to a silver skull like a Spielberg Hamlet – to ensure the most dizzying and future-facing of stadium spectacles. At its climax, a giant alien borg bursts from the stage, flailing at the air, growing angrier as Stockholm Syndrome mashes magnificently into Reapers and New Born. Keep telling yourself: it's only a simulation… • At Ashton Gate stadium, Bristol, 5 June; and touring.

Text2: No 6, the Prisoner-themed festival season closer held in the bijou Italianate village of Portmeirion, produced unlikely heroes: the security guard cajoled into joining the impromptu ukulele orchestra on the ornate colonnade; the Tron drum troupe leading Saturday's dusk procession and their robot marchers, neon tubes on every limb; the 50s housewives singing calypso tunes from a dinghy in the fountains and the Brythonthiaid male voice choir, welcomed to the piazza stage for their choral covers of Chic, New Order and Muse so rapturously you'd think David Bowie had joined. Festival No 6 is the first UK festival where the canvas is as important as its contents. This second year, the spectacle has expanded from Prisoner recreations to hallucinogenic carnivals and pop-up performance pieces. Only the most imaginative bands competed with the stunning setting. Neon Neon accompanied their 80s electro-flashdances with footage of communist luminaries and signs that read "Resist Phoney Encores". Public Service Broadcasting built electro-rock squalls around antique newsreel announcements, right down to their prerecorded audience banter. On Friday, headliner James Blake created the future of soul by imagining the xx fronted by Antony Hegarty. Representing the ultimate monstrous evolution of the guitar, My Bloody Valentine headlined on Saturday, their vocal subtleties sacrificed for churning volume. Some people ran screaming from noise tornados mischievously titled things like Only Tomorrow and Softly Mauve, others basked in the violent, amorphous magnificence of the song Soon, which resembles Pet Shop Boys cast into hellfire. The 10-minute holochord segment of You Made Me Realise was one endurance test too far for many in the audience. Another endurance test came on Sunday, when howling winds and rainstorms closed secondary tents. Survivors were treated to an encore of hits; a smattering of Smiths from Johnny Marr, Chic's disco inferno and Manic Street Preachers, whose comeback show mirrored their career by flip-flopping between genius and mundanity. Roaring punk classics Motorcycle Emptiness, Revol and You Love Us gave way to slippered stumbles from their acoustic-led new album Rewind the Film, saved only by Richard Hawley's charmed guest spot. A damp finale, but the magic of No 6 remains unquenched.

So far, the Lucknow couple have managed to cover three of the six World Marathon Majors - New York, Chicago, and London - and will create history on April 17 by participating in the Boston marathon, completing four major marathon loops.
"Both  Asha  and I had the keen desire to either run or do something physically challenging but never expressed it while our children were growing up," said Col Singh.
When their children got settled, they thought it was their golden chance to give wings to their desire. "It was a 10 kilometre run and without any practice, we somehow got reasonably high standing. We were motivated to take the fast lane in amateur running," said Asha.
Married for 40 years, they have already earned the honour of being the first married couple from India to hit the track for a global marathon and for making it to the International Book of World Records for being the only married couple to run three World Marathon Majors together. 
"After several 10km runs where we had podium finishes, we graduated to half-marathon. Not satisfied, I ran a full marathon in Goa. Asha was unhappy as I did not agree to her trying a full marathon," recalled Col Singh. Months later, the couple ran their first full marathon in Hyderabad. "I was the only woman to run a full marathon in the senior veteran category and was very excited. Now, we are participating in marathon races all over the country," Asha said.
Difference in their personalities is evident in their training style. While Asha loves distance, her husband prefers speed. "Asha is stronger, both physically and mentally. During training, I focus on quality, she prefers quantity. I eat well, she eats frugally. I am a non-vegetarian, she is a vegetarian. I spend a lot while she believes in saving. The common thread between us is that we both take up challenges," said Col Singh. "Both of us want to do better and not compete with each other. Asha is a bit more competitive than I am. Text2: Lucknow: The faculty and student attendance marking system in  government schools  is all set to undergo a complete change with use of technology to maintain accurate daily records. The department of education will, in a pilot project, begin marking attendance of teachers and students online, using tablets, from November 20. 
The pilot will be conducted in seven districts, comprising Lucknow, Hardoi, Lakhimpur Kheri, Rae Bareli, Sitapur, Unnao, and Shravasti.The move comes after the department developed a new module of digitising 12 registers including teacher and student attendance register maintained by state-run schools on its Prerna portal. With this, the department is encouraging primary schools to adopt a smart working style to enhance transparency and do away with data manipulation. Teachers will mark their attendance twice on the portal using their mobile numbers. 
In summers, from April 1 to September 30, teachers would mark attendance between 7.45am and 8 am and between 2.15pm and 2.30 pm. In winters-from October 1 to March 31-the window for marking attendance will be 8.45am to 9 am, and 3.15 to 3.30 pm. Teachers' attendance will be certified by the head teacher. Daily attendance for students will be marked between 8am and 9 am and between 9 am and 10 am, in summers and winters, respectively. The tablets provided to schools are geo-fenced to ensure attendance is marked from within the school premises. 
Director general of school education (DGSE) Vijay Kiran Anand said, "Each school is being provided two tablets to push high quality digital content and lesson plans, to monitor classroom transactions and gather information about student and teacher attendance. This will improve learning outcomes of students." 
With the digitisation process, the manual registers will be preserved as archives at the school level. "The process of digitisation of registers is undertaken to ensure the system is real time and transparent and reduce the administrative burden of teachers so that they can spend more time on academic work. This in turn will help improve governance manifold," Anand said.

Text1: The long, easy days of summer are all but behind us; we're heading quickly into autumn and back to the day-to-day. For some, it's a welcome return to routine, but for me, someone who spends their life trying to side-step routine, it's always a bit of a downer. When I was a kid, my mum would soften the blow with a new pencil case or lunchbox. Now, I cook. These recipes are the kind I make on a Sunday with leftovers on purpose that I'll be able to use a few ways throughout the week, to make this return a little smoother. The mole is the kind of recipe which takes a bit of love, but ends up with the most rich, rounded and deeply fruity chilli sauce, which you can use to flavour roast veg, beans in tacos, burritos or as a traditional mole stew. The homemade flour tortillas work perfectly with the mole, but can also be heated up through the week. Ancho chilli and peanut mole This recipe makes four portions of the mole sauce: one to use in the recipe with the roast veg, and three to store in the fridge or freezer to use for a quick-from-the-freezer dinner (ideas below). Whole, dried ancho chillies are available from most supermarkets in the spice section. If you can't get your hands on them, you could use a heaped teaspoon of dried chilli flakes instead. Prep 15 min Soak 20 min Cook 1 hr Serves 4 (plus extra sauceleftover mole sauce for three more dinners) For the mole 4 dried ancho chillies, seeds and stems removed, or 1 heaped tsp dried chilli flakes 1 onion, peeled and quartered 3 garlic cloves, peeled 3 vine tomatoes Flaky salt 2 tbsp chipotle paste 60g dark chocolate (70%), broken into squares 75g peanuts 75g almonds 50g pumpkin seeds 1 tsp cumin seeds 75g raisins 25g sesame seeds 750ml vegetable stock For the roast veg 750g new potatoes, larger ones cut in half 400g banana shallots, peeled and halved ½ butternut squash (about 500g), cut into large chunks 2 corn on the cob, kernels cut from the cob Olive oil To serve Fresh coriander Tortillas Juice of 1 lime Remove the seeds and stems from the dried ancho chillies, then lightly toast the chillies in a dry frying pan, being careful not to burn them. Remove the chillies from the pan, put in a bowl of boiling water and soak for 20 minutes – if you are using dried red chilli flakes instead, just toast them (there's no need to soak). Bring a medium saucepan of water to a boil, then add the onion, garlic, tomatoes and a good pinch of salt. Turn down the heat and simmer for 10 minutes, or until the skins on the tomatoes start to come away and the onions are soft. Drain (retaining the chilli water), and put the solids in a high-speed blender with 200ml of the saved water and the chipotle paste. Blend really smooth, then, while still warm, add the chocolate and stir to melt. Set aside. Toast the nuts, pumpkin seeds, cumin seeds and raisins in the same pan you toasted the ancho chilli in: you want them to be golden and well-toasted, so don't be afraid to take them a little further than you usually would. Text1: Paul Miller is almost single-handedly keeping the Shavian flame alive. This is his fourth production of one of the plays in five years and it induces in the audience a giddy delight that reminds me of the comment by Jorge Luis Borges that the work of Shaw "leaves one with a flavour of liberation". That liberation takes many forms in this remarkable play, first performed in 1895. For a start, we see the eponymous heroine exposing the word-drunk absurdity of the two men competing for her love: her Christian socialist husband, Rev Morell, and the hyperbolic teenage poet, Marchbanks. When Claire Lams's spritely, mischievous Candida mockingly asks them "pray, my lords and masters, what have you to offer for my choice?" we could be watching a comedic version of Ibsen. But Miller has also grasped that there is something Dionysiac within Shaw. Far from being the desiccated brainbox people assume, he writes about the extremes of passion. Four of the characters are here described as mad and there is a wildness to the play that comes out beautifully in this production. You see that in Martin Hutson's violently hot-tempered Morell who, after Candida has attempted to soothe his ruffled feelings, turns on her and cries: "I had rather you had plunged a grappling iron into my heart than given me that kiss." Joseph Potter, making an impressive stage debut, captures Marchbanks's frantic impulsiveness while suggesting that, like so many of Shaw's characters, he is doomed to a martyred solitude. All three leads are first-rate, but one test of a good Shaw production is that all the characters are buoyantly alive. Michael Simkins gives a richly funny performance as Candida's grasping father, showing how an unscrupulous, exploitative businessman sees himself as a model of practical common-sense. Sarah Middleton captures perfectly the unrequited passion of Morell's adoring secretary who, after breaking her non-drinking habit, announces: "I'm only a beer teetotaller, not a champagne teetotaller." Miller's production, which shows a rare understanding of Shaw, itself has the sparkle of vintage fizz. • At Orange Tree, Richmond upon Thames, until 11 January.

Text1: Mumbai: Observing that the need for bigger space for a landlord's family members was genuine, the  Bombay high court  upheld orders directing a tenant to vacate premises in a building in Bhuleshwar in south Mumbai.
"…the landlord is the best judge of his  residential requirement  and the tenant cannot dictate terms to him as to how he can and how he should adjust in the available premises,'' said Justice Anuja Prabhudessai.
In May 2004, the landlords/owners – Chandrakant, Ketan and Sanjiv Shah – issued a notice to Hasmukh Shah terminating the tenancy and asked him to vacate the 319 sq ft premises in Liladhar Mansion. His cousin Ajay Shah replied stating that he was in possession of the premises and was using it as his residence-cum-office.
The landlords filed an eviction suit that the premises were unauthorisedly sublet by Hasmukh to Ajay. Their 11 family members were residing in about 400 sq ft carpet area and faced space constraints. Denying the subletting to him, Ajay said the premises were originally occupied by his father and uncle since 1954. Also, the landlords have more than sufficient residence space.
 In February 2020, the Small Causes Court passed an eviction order on the ground of reasonable and bonafide requirement of the landlords. The appellate bench confirmed the order. Justice Prabhudessai said Maharashtra Rent Control Act,1999 provides for eviction of a tenant on the ground of reasonable and bonafide requirement of the landlord. Also while the burden of proving the same lies with the landlord, the tenant must establish greater hardship to resist eviction. 
She noted that Hasmukh's evidence revealed he left the premises in 1961-62. Ajay resides in an ownership flat and has a tenanted room in Ghatkopar. It was not his case that there are no office premises available in the vicinity. Justice Prabhudessai said the proven fact is that the need of the landlords "is genuine, honest and conceived in good faith and thus reasonable and bonafide." She granted Ajay three months to vacate.

Text2: Mumbai:  Bombay high court  on Monday dismissed a petition by builder Lalit Tekchandani seeking to club and quash first information reports (FIR) registered against him for allegedly duping more than 1,700 flat purchasers in a housing project in Taloja, Navi Mumbai.
"We are not inclined to grant relief. For reasons to be recorded separately, the petition is dismissed," Justice Prakash Naik and Justice Nitin Borkar said.
Tekchandani's petition said that in 2010 a 15-acre land piece in Rohinjan village was given by owner Narendra Bhalla to directors of  Supreme Constructions  and Developers Pvt Ltd.In 2012,  construction  commenced on nine towers. In 2016, Tekchandani resigned as a director. The due date for handing over possession of flats was Dec 31, 2017. In Jan 2017 investors began questioning the delay and were given various reasons. On Jan 15 this year, FIRs were registered by Chembur and Taloja police stations. 
Tekchandani was booked for criminal breach of trust and cheating. On Jan 30, the Economic Offences Wing took over the Chembur FIR and arrested him. His petition said he was innocent and concocted FIRs had been registered against him.
Prosecutor Mankunwar Deshmukh said there were 1,712 flat purchasers who invested Rs 423 crore. "It is not a small amount. Under his directorship investment was made by customers. Whether he resigned or not, makes no difference. The deadline (to give possession of flats) was 2017. We are in 2024," she said.
Deshmukh said the amount collected was diverted elsewhere. Also, Tekchandani bought personal properties, gave loans on interest and mortgaged flats promised to Bhalla. She opposed merging of FIRs, saying complainants, flats, court jurisdictions and police commissionerates were different.
Tekchandani's advocate, Taraq Sayed, said that Supreme was unable to complete the project because of pending litigation with Bhalla.
He said amounts which came to Tekchandani's account from flat purchasers were accounted for and went into construction. "Till the time I was director the project was well on course … . Let them investigate. I feel for them (purchasers) also," he said. He said that another FIR was registered in Taloja.
Advocate Subir Sarkar, for complainant Ganesh Bisht in the Taloja FIR, said: "He is still servicing the loan he had taken and there is no end in sight." Advocate Himanshu Kode, for Clan City Welfare Association, said: "Till date, except for false assurance and cheating, nothing is done."

Text1: Chennaiyin FC (CFC) will aim to continue their winning momentum when they host a beleaguered SC East Bengal side in the ISL at the Tilak Maidan on Friday.
While two-time champions CFC have begun their campaign with wins in both their matches so far, everything has gone wrong for their opponents. The red and gold brigade has had a horrid start with two losses and a draw but what will be more distressing for their coach Manolo Diaz is the amount of goals – 10 – they have conceded in these matches.
Diaz admitted that defence is a concern for his team. "We are not comfortable defending free-kicks and set-pieces. We are working on it. Not only the defenders, but the entire team needs to stay focused throughout the match if we are to do well," the Spaniard said during a virtual pre-match media conference on Thursday.
CFC coach Bozidar Bandovic said that he has made note of East Bengal's defensive frailties. "We are aware of East Bengal's weaknesses but we are not taking them lightly. We are preparing in the same way like we do for other teams with full discipline and focus. After three losses, East Bengal will be desperate to win and want to make a comeback. So we need to be ready," Bandovic said. 
Despite winning both their matches, Chennaiyin have taken time to settle down and often looked sluggish. Their modus operandi has been to hold their defensive shape and launch quick counter-attacks. 
Bandovic said that his wards need to improve both tactically and physically. "My players need to be quicker. I want them to train their minds and stay focused so that they can make good decisions during crucial moments. If you have possession and are attacking but not creating any chances, then possession doesn't mean anything to me. At the same time, without a good defence, we don't have a team. Physically, I want my players to be fresh till the final whistle. So far, I am happy with how my players have reacted and we are looking to build on it," said Bandovic. 
While CFC will look to pile misery on East Bengal, the 53-year-old Diaz said he wants his players to learn from his mistakes and focus on the positives. East Bengal might have conceded six goals in their last match against Odisha but have also scored four. "The fact that we have started scoring goals is a big positive. It is an indication of the fact that the attacking line-up has started clicking together. But in football, it is a matter of balance," said Diaz. 
There are no fitness concerns for Chennaiyin while East Bengal are still sweating on the fitness of their goalkeeper Arindam Bhattacharya and defender Adil Khan.

Text2: In 1894, a respectable and apparently meek woman did something many contemporaries would have regarded as astonishing, if not deplorable. She stood for election to the district council against two male candidates, including a vicar. When Lady Laura Ridding, wife of a bishop, won an election in which women had no vote, she became the first female guardian of the local workhouse, Southwell in Nottinghamshire. "She was a remarkable woman, our Laura, and having got herself elected she really was a force for change," said Jan Overfield Shaw, a community officer at the Victorian workhouse. "She did what none of the male guardians did: she saw what could really make a difference to the lives of the women here – including better food and proper underwear. "The bishop was much older than her, and he looks a bit dry in official portraits – but he supported her work for women's rights." Southwell is one of the best-preserved workhouses in the country and is now owned by the National Trust. Ridding's photograph, which shows her gazing up at her fiance, has just gone on display among portraits of the suffragists and suffragettes she joined in the campaign for votes for women. The exhibition, created by the National Trust and the National Portrait Gallery, is in the former committee room of the workhouse, where between 1894 and 1905 Ridding worked with the other guardians. Ridding, an author whose works include three volumes of her husband's biography, was already a founder member of the National Union of Women Workers, an umbrella organisation for voluntary philanthropy. The exhibition reflects divisions at the time. Octavia Hill, the co-founder of the National Trust, wrote to the Times in 1910 saying "a serious loss to our country would arise if women entered political life". She shares the walls with the Pankhursts; Mary Raleigh Richardson, who slashed Velázquez's Rokeby Venus in the National Gallery to publicise the campaign; and the actor Ellen Terry, who supported votes for women but wrote: "The Suffragettes are a magnificent lot of women but I think perhaps their ardour carries them away at times." Ridding, though never a window-smashing militant, would ardently support the campaign after her own small victory in the local election. Newly transcribed diaries show her worrying about small details that could make the everyday life of the inmates wretched or relatively content: the meat she tasted one day was stringy and unpleasant, she noted, and the pudding was "great lumpy suet with treacle". Text1: The embattled House intelligence committee chairman, Devin Nunes, has refused to recuse himself from the committee's investigation into Donald Trump's ties to Russia, despite calls from Democrats. "Why would I?" asked Nunes, who has lost the confidence of the Democrats on the intelligence committee after a series of allegations that they consider a cover-up for the White House. "It's the same thing as always around this place: a lot of politics, people get heated, but I'm not going to involve myself with that." The speaker of the House gave Nunes his full confidence on Tuesday. Asked at a press conference whether he should step down, Paul Ryan, the most senior Republican in Congress, responded simply: "No." With the Republicans generally united in defense of the inquiry, chances are diminishing for its work to be accepted as definitive. The Republicans are also blocking the establishment of an independent commission into ties between the Trump campaign and Russia. Doubts over Nunes sharply escalated after the California Republican canceled a public hearing originally planned for Tuesday during which two senior intelligence officials appointed by Barack Obama, and the former acting attorney general Sally Yates, were scheduled to testify. Yates, whom Trump fired after she refused to defend his travel ban in court, was reportedly told by the Trump administration that her testimony was subject to constraint. The Washington Post published letters from Yates's attorney indicating the justice department informed her that "all information Ms Yates received or actions she took" while a senior department official represented "client confidences that she may not disclose absent written consent of the Department". The justice department's client is the United States, not the president. Sean Spicer, the White House press secretary, disputed the story, calling it "entirely false". "The White House has taken no action to prevent Sally Yates from testifying and the Department of Justice specifically told her that it would not stop her, and to suggest otherwise is completely irresponsible," Spicer said. In his press briefing, Spicer said the White House had no objection to Yates's testimony and denied any coordination with Nunes to block it. "I hope she testifies. I look forward to it," Spicer said. It was the latest controversy shadowing Nunes. Last week, following a public hearing that undermined Trump's evidence-free claim that Obama put him under surveillance, Nunes said he was "alarmed" to learn of documents indicating Trump allies had their communications incidentally collected as part of "lawful" surveillance. He did not disclose until Monday that he received those documents not in the committee's secured workspaces for viewing classified material, but at the White House complex. Text2: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister  Narendra Modi  is set to inaugurate and lay  foundation stones  for approximately 100  NH projects  worth around Rs 1 lakh crore on March 11 (Monday) when he throws open the  Dwarka Expressway  stretch in Haryana. 
The govt is also likely to clear major proposals in its next Cabinet meeting on Tuesday, which would perhaps be the last in PM's second tenure.
Sources said the NH projects for which PM will lay foundation stones include Bengaluru-Vijayawada expressway entailing Rs 14,000 crore, Belgaum-Raichur highway (Rs 8,000 cr) and Shamli-Ambala highway (Rs 5,000 cr). The projects, which will be inaugurated, include the two packages of Dwarka Expressway, Kiratpur-Ner Chowk in Himachal Pradesh and Narayanpur-Purnea stretch in Bihar.
"This will be one of the biggest programmes when in one day so many projects will be opened to the public and foundation stones will be laid," said a source. They added that the PM is also likely to launch several highway projects in the North East when he inaugurates the Sela tunnel in Arunachal Pradesh on Saturday.
On Tuesday, Modi will also virtually flag off around a dozen  Vande Bharat trains  during his visit to Gujarat. A host of other railway projects will be inaugurated as well, sources said. 
Last week, the PM had asked secretaries of departments to expedite the finalisations of plans so that foundation stone laying and inauguration of infrastructure projects can be done by March 12.

Text1: MUMBAI: On Tuesday, when 17 states together would borrow a little over  Rs 50,000 crore  through  auction  of  bonds , it would be the highest such  borrowing  amount on a single day either by central or state govts in India's bond market history. The record high amount, however, is unlikely to disrupt the prevailing yields in the market given the way  RBI  and central govt together have managed the  gilt auctions  this fiscal, bond dealers and fund managers said.
In recent times, the highest amount raised from a single-day gilt auction was on Feb 2 this year when central govt borrowed Rs 39,000 crore.
On Friday, March 15, RBI announced that 17 state govts together would borrow Rs 50,206 crore through auctions on Tuesday, March 19. Of the 17, at Rs 8,000 crore, UP is slotted to be the biggest borrower, followed by Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu, at Rs 6,000 crore each.
The higher borrowing amounts by state govts came in the absence of borrowing by central govt after Feb 15 as there is robust long-term domestic  investor demand  owing to jump in investable flows towards the end of the fiscal.
This is reflected in the spread between yields on state govt bonds and central govt bonds (gilts). From a spread of more than 50 basis points (100bps = 1 percentage point) on 10-year state bonds over 10-year gilts about two months ago, it has come down to 35bps. And this happened despite higher borrowing by state govts.
This difference could get narrower. "Considering the softening outlook of the interest rate and history of much lower state borrowing during the first quarter of the fiscal, the spread between state govt bonds and gilts is expected compress over the next quarter," said Ram Kamal Samanta, senior VP – investment, Star Union Dai-ichi Life Insurance.

Text2: Fischer-Saidy USA Ch. 1966. White to move. RB This week the boot is on the other foot and it's Dan's turn to puzzle over the position. I chose this position because in some ways it seems a very unFischer-like game. Among the legendary former world champion's most notable qualities were clarity and control. It's hard to see those qualities at work here. In fact – is it treasonable to suggest? – this looks like the kind of position amateurs like me might stumble into. Let's see what the grandmaster makes of it. DK The Fischer games I selected for Ronan over the previous few weeks are, I think, typical of his style: pieces working in harmony and clear-cut strategies. But this looks a mess. Black has just advanced the e-pawn and if the knight retreats – let's say 1 Nb3 – I don't see what's wrong with 1...Qxc2. No, that can't be right. White must not back down, even if it means giving up material. In keeping with Fischer's style, I'm looking for clarity, so let's ignore the threat to the knight and chop a path through to the king: 1 Bxh5 Nxh5 2 Rxh5 exd4 3 Bxd4 seems more or less forced. At a stroke, White's pieces look fantastic and I can see some tasty tactics. If 3...Bb7 4 Qe2 (threatening Qe6+) Be4 5 Rh7 and Qh5. What about 3...Rf7...? I can't quite see how to crack it. Maybe 4 Rh6...? Or the flashy 4 Qh4...? Something has to work. I've seen enough – 1 Bxh5 has to be the way forward. RB Damn! He got it. I, of course, was worried by the knight d4 and looked at 1 Nb3 and 1 Nf3. But both moves hardly do anything for White's initiative. After 1 Nb3, Black can continue to develop with 1...Bb7 or maybe even 1...Ne6, while after 1 Nf3, what's to stop Black grabbing a pawn with 1...Nxf4...? Bf3 is another alternative, and I'm not sure what to make of the position after 1...exd4 2 Bxa8 dxe3. Next week we announce the first nomination for our annual chess book of the year award. Text2: BAREILLY: A 23-year-old man, who was looking after his crop field, was allegedly sexually assaulted by three men at a village in Sambhal district. The accused men also shot a  video  of the crime and later shared it on social media.
The  farmer 's parents approached the police and lodged an FIR under IPC sections 377 (unnatural offences) and 506 (criminal intimidation) along with section 67 of the IT Act on Thursday evening.
"We've arrested one of the accused. Two still at large. The man was assaulted on January 7. He was threatened to remain quiet. He is still in a state of trauma," said police.
According to locals, the man, who is married, stayed in the farm to save standing crops from stray cattle when the accused assaulted him. On Thursday, a purported video was shared on social media and it came to the notice of the man's family.
SHO, Rajpura, Amrit Lal said on Friday, "We've recorded the man's statement after registering the FIR. Medico-legal examination has confirmed the assault." Police said the three had assaulted the man earlier as well and "the crime is being investigated".

Text2: Theresa May has insisted that her government looks "more like the country it serves" after axing a string of white men in their 50s and 60s while promoting a number of younger, female and minority ethnic MPs. The prime minister used the second day of her new year reshuffle to refresh the lower ministerial ranks after a difficult cabinet-level shake-up in which some ministers resisted attempts to move them. In a blow to May's authority, Justine Greening quit the government after refusing to take up a position at the helm of the Department for Work and Pensions and Jeremy Hunt persuaded the prime minister he should remain in a beefed-up role as secretary for health and social care – a decision that the Guardian understands scuppered Downing Street's original plan to appoint Greg Clark as the new health secretary. May was left facing criticism for sacking one female, gay minister, while giving in to male colleagues and failing to promote ethnic minorities. Moreover, the Sutton Trust published an analysis claiming the new top team was more privileged than before, with more than a third who those who will be attending cabinet educated privately (five times the figure for the overall population) while almost half studied at Oxbridge. Four of the 10 women attending meetings are not full members of cabinet, which means May's leading team has a gender pay gap with men earning on average £138,688, 11% more than the women at £124,758. May's moves on Tuesday boosted the number of women in government from 30 to 37 and the number of ethnic minorities from four to nine. With almost 120 members of the government altogether, that means female representation has risen from 25% but is still just 30%. However, the move was criticised in some quarters of her party. MP Philip Davies, who is known for his controversial anti-feminist views but who sits on parliament's women and equalities committee, said there was now "a legitimate concern that some people may feel they have been hoofed out or not promoted simply because they are a white male". MP Michael Fabricant praised the promotions , but raised concerns about men being described as "pale and stale". May made clear that she did not believe that ability had been compromised at all, insisting the reshuffle brought in "fresh talent" that would help her focus on key areas such as housing, health and social care. "It also allows a new generation of gifted ministers to step up and make life better for people across the whole UK," she said. Among those promoted were MPs seen as rising stars within Conservative ranks such as Dominic Raab, who took over at housing, Alok Sharma, the new employment minister, Caroline Dinenage at health and Margot James, who moved to the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport. Text1: Nagpur: Every time a train passes Dewhadi village, the doors of a Kaali Mata temple are closed by the priest. "Otherwise, the diyas inside the temple will get extinguished," says the priest. Wondering how a train can extinguish a lamp? It can happen easily if the train is zooming past just a few inches away from the temple
The Kaali Mata temple inside Tumsar Road Railway station in Dewhadi, 80km from Nagpur, is the only temple in India situated between railway tracks, nestling between platform Nos.3 and 4.
The temple, constructed during the British era, sees an increased footfall during Navratri. "All your wishes get fulfilled here if you pray with all your heart," says Sushma Bilankar, a local.
The temple has a lot of folklore attached to it. As per the British record, the first train of Nagpur division ran in the year 1881 between Nagpur and Dewhadi. Soon after, the Britishers wanted to extend the railway line further.
Around 25,000 pine sleepers were brought from England to speed up the process of laying railway tracks. Labourers and railway employees from Bengal too were summoned to Dewhadi.
It is here that the story gets interesting. When unearthing was being done on the planned route, the labourers were not able to move four stones laid next to each other at a particular spot above which the railway track was to be laid.
Heavy machinery was pressed into action for the following seven days but the stones could not be moved.
"My grandmother told me that some of the workers who were assigned the job claimed that they saw Kaali Mata in their dreams. The goddess told them not to uproot the stones. Even the chief railway officer at that time, who had the same dream, had said that moving the stones would result in destruction," says Vishal Parihar, a techie from Dewhadi who now works in Pune.
"The workers were so frightened that they requested the Britishers to alter the route of the railway track just a bit," he adds.
The Britishers, locals say, gave up the idea to uproot the stones after which the Bengal labourers and railway employees constructed a small temple between the tracks.
A few years down the line, local devotees installed a beautiful idol of the goddess and reconstructed the temple. Call it superstition or faith, but the temple has many followers. The temple sees locals, passengers and railway employees coming to worship regularly.
The Tumsar Road railway station, on the Mumbai-Howrah route, is one of the busiest stations in South East Central Railway with 84 trains passing through it. "Many times, we have to wait if there is a train stationed at platform No. 1. Sometimes it happens that we are stuck in front of the temple with trains stationed at platform Nos. 3 and 4. But we don't mind," said a local.

Text2: NAGPUR: After more than three years since the battle for the supremacy between Hockey India and the Indian Hockey Federation started, the fate of over 1500 hockey players of Vidarbha is hanging by a thread and they are clueless about the happenings in the administration. 
The Vidarbha Hockey Association, which is affiliated to Indian Hockey Federation (IHF) along with Mumbai, Maharashtra, Bhopal and Hyderabad, is fighting a three-year long fight with Hockey India (HI) and International Hockey Federation (FIH) for its survival.However, the top bosses of the VHA believe that the sportspersons' future is in safe hands. 
After IHF was disbanded and HI took over the reins in 2008, the existence of VHA and other associations was in danger as HI adhered to one-state-one-unit policy. However, Delhi High Court's judgement last year cleared the cloud of suspension hovering over IHF. 
"The judgement to reinstate IHF meant that the body is allowed to conduct the national-level and government tournaments. So, that was a big boost for our players," VHA secretary Vinod Gavai told TOI on Tuesday. 
The only huddle for IHF is its non-recognition by the international body (FIH). The IHF has also filed a case against FIH a year ago challenging its decision to derecognize all the bodies associated with it. "We are still awaiting a decision on the same. How can they just disaffiliate a six-decade old body such as VHA. However, as for now, we are happy that our players are getting a chance to participate in the national level tournaments," Gavai added. 
Gavai also lashed out at HI and its ways of running the sport in the country. "They only have a pool of 50-60 senior players to choose from. Ultimately, it's the players who are getting hampered," he said. 
Amid the hullabaloo, the players feel they are at the receiving end. "We still don't know what's going on. There are so many people who advice us and they have equally different versions about the issue. As players, our career span is so little. If we'll be just figuring out as to whom to play under, when will we play," said a player not wanting to be named.

Text1: LUCKNOW: Governor Anandiben Patel re-appointed Lucknow University vice-chancellor professor  Alok Kumar Rai  as the new VC of the varsity on Friday. Prof Rai became the second VC post-Independence to get a second term.
It is after 54 years that a VC will be working for six years in a row. Apart from this, Prof Rai has also added his name to history by becoming a VC of the first state university that has an A++ grade in the National Assessment Accreditation Council (NAAC).
He will also be remembered for heading the university in its centennial year and for conducting the 100-year celebrations. The decision brought a wave of happiness to the LU campus for teachers and students who were anticipating that Prof Rai will get a second term.
15 had applied for VC's post
Professor Rai joined as LU VC on December 30, 2019. His three-year tenure ended Friday and all eyes were on Raj Bhawan for the last few days for the appointment of the university VC.
Governor Anandiben Patel, who is also the chancellor of the state universities, gave final assent on the name of the VC out of the names recommended by the search committee. Around 15 academicians who had applied for the VC's post were screened by the search committee. Thereafter, three academicians, including Prof Rai and one from Gorakhpur and Gujarat each, were interviewed.
Sources at Raj Bhawan told TOI that the selection process got delayed as the vice-chancellor of Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj University, Kanpur, Professor Vinay Pathak, who is allegedly facing corruption charges, was one of three members of the search committee.
Recently, Raj Bhawan removed Prof Pathak from the search committee and brought academician Anand K Tyagi in his place.
The LU's executive council had sent the name of the vice-chancellor of Gujarat Central University, Prof Rama Shanker Dubey, as the second member while the third member is a judge from the high court. Raj Bhawan had advertised for the post on October 11 this year.

Text2: Lucknow: A team of the  National Assessment Accreditation Council  (NAAC) will visit  Lucknow University  on July 11 for a re-assessment. The NAAC inspection will continue till July 13.
While names of NAAC team members will be announced three-four days prior to their visit, the news of the NAAC inspection has triggered hectic activities on the campus with the faculty and varsity officials stepping up their efforts to come out with flying colours.
The university's main gate has been locked so that preparations are not interrupted by outsiders and a strict checking was done of all entry and exit points.
The day begins with LU vice-chancellor  Prof Alok Kumar Rai  making a visit to every department along with representatives of the Internal Quality Assurance Cell and senior administrative officials. During the inspection the VC and his team ensure that nothing is left to chance. Special focus is being laid on cleanliness, student facility and maintenance of records.
"We are well prepared for the NAAC visit, but there is always scope for improvement, it's like making your home look more beautiful when a guest arrives. The VC has inspected commerce department,  NSS office , proctor office, public administration department and office of the  Lucknow University Athletic Association  and suggested ways to improve it," a senior university official said. He added that on the VC's suggestions they have already set up a wall of fame and an achievers' gallery, displaying names and photos of students leading top organizations in the country and abroad.

Text1: NEW DELHI: A week after notifying the  Green Credit Programme  ( GCP ) for promoting environment-friendly practices across the country, the  environment ministry  has come out with two separate draft methodologies for generating such credits through water harvesting and tree plantation projects in different states/UTs, and buying/ selling it through a centrally-managed dedicated platform.
The ministry in its drafts, released last week seeking suggestions or objections from stakeholders, lists state/district-wise appropriate water conservation/ harvesting structures like earthen ponds and poly tanks, and tree/ horticulture species which can be picked up for actions by individuals/ cooperatives or urban/rural local bodies.
Their actions will generate green credits (GCs) through specified calculations based on a physical verification process. For example, 100 GCs will be distributed to eligible applicants for 10 years for 100 trees. "Plantation of minimum 100 trees will be required for qualifying under tree plantation based Green Credit," said the draft on tree plantation projects, noting that minimum 100 trees per hectare and maximum 1,000 trees per hectare will be required to be planted.
Similarly for generating green credits (GCs) for water harvesting structures based on site location, the minimum size/storage capacity of water conservation/harvesting structures will be 100 cubic metre or 1 lakh litre and maximum size of 10,000 cubic metre. Individuals/entities can get 75 GCs per 100 cubic metre after completion of specified number of years.
The GCP is an innovative market-based mechanism designed to incentivise voluntary environmental actions. Its notification ahead of the upcoming UN climate conference (COP28) assumes significance as it reflects India's approach of addressing environmental concerns under its Mission LiFE - Lifestyle for Environment - which was launched last year as a grass-root mass movement for protection and conservation of environment and for other environmental and climate gains.
Individuals and entities will have to register their activities through the central government's dedicated app/website to obtain green credits. The administrator will verify the activity through a designated agency. Once verification is complete, the administrator will grant a  green credit  certificate which will be tradable on the green credit platform.
The notification said that the GCP is independent of the carbon credit under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, 2023. It noted that since an environmental activity generating green credit may have climate co-benefits, such as reduction or removal of carbon emissions, the GCP may also get carbon credit from the same activity under the Scheme.

Text2: MUMBAI: The Bombay high court on Tuesday asked the BMC if it could ban the entry of RTI activists and users from entering civic buildings. "These are public institutions and you may be well within its right to regulate entry. We can understand if some areas are restricted. But can you ban entry completely? This is like externing a person from the area," remarked a division bench of Chief Justice Naresh Patil and Justice Makarand Karnik.The bench said that it was going by the petitioners' claims that the entry of activists had been banned.
The court was hearing a public interest litigation filed by activist Kamlakar Shenoy against the BMC and municipal commissioner Ajoy Mehta for allegedly calling RTI users "extortionists" and "blackmailers."
Advocate Aditya Bhat, counsel for the petitioner, said that in K West ward, the corporation had put up display boards with the photographs of activists, saying they were "professional complainants" and their entry was barred.
In an affidavit, the BMC justified the statements made by Mehta. The affidavit said that the "municipal commissioner had full right to intimate or to make a statement in public regarding issues involving larger public interest which are acting as a hindrance in the fulfilment of the duties of the corporation and causing mental and physical inconvenience to the general public due to oral and written submissions by unrelated and unaffected entities". The BMC further said that it had issued a circular to streamline its working so that grievances of the citizens can be redressed.
Advocate Bhatt pointed out that as per the figures provided by the corporation, of the around 41,550 complaints received by the 24 wards, 37,632 had been classified as being filed by those not personally affected.
The petitioner claimed that there was no provision in the rules that categorised complainants as affected or unaffected parties and this was a ploy to deny information. The petitioner further alleged that attempts were being made to frustrate the provisions of the Right to Information Act.
"It appears that the BMC is prejudiced against any form of civic activism which in fact causes hindrance to the illegal acts of the officials of the corporation and seeks to protect offenders. The issuance of such statements and framing of undemocratic policies by the municipal commissioner will suppress civic activism and alert citizens who act as watchdogs. It will promote corruption," the petitioner said.
The high court has asked BMC to take further instructions and scheduled the matter for further hearing after four weeks.

Text1: BHUBANESHWAR:  Vaccine manufacturing plant  Sapigen Biologix at  Odisha Biotech Park , Andharua, here will start  commercial production  by May this year. VK Pandian, chairman 5T and Nabin Odisha, said this after visiting the plant on Sunday. 
Official sources said the plant will have a capacity to produce 2.4 crore doses of different vaccines per day. It is in its final phase of commissioning."With its full capacity, this facility in Odisha will be the biggest vaccine producing plant in the country," it added. 
This plant led by Dr Krishna Ella of Bharat Biotech is coming up with an investment of Rs 1500 crores. It will create 1500 direct employment, and most of them are being hired locally from Odisha. The plant plans to produce 15 plus different vaccines for diseases like cholera and malaria, said the official statement of chief minister's office (CMO).
"These vaccines will be supplied to many parts of the world. It will strengthen the name for Odisha in the field of biotechnology. With vaccines from here, millions of lives will be safeguarded around the world," said Pandian. 
He visited all the subunits of the plant and interacted with the management and employees and instructed all govt agencies to assist in the commissioning of the plant within the next three months. 
Pandian has assured all help from the government. He expressed confidence that with this large anchor manufacturing plant, many other complementary biotechnology related product companies will get attracted to the Odisha Biotech Park, bringing major investments and creating jobs in this speciality field.
Odisha govt has recently approved biotechnology policy.

Text2: BHUBANESWAR:  Indian Railways  has sanctioned  Rs 197 crore  for the  redevelopment  of  Balasore railway station . Railway minister  Ashwini Vaishnaw  said this in a social media post on Friday. 
According to the Railways, the station's design integrates elements like arches, ornate facades, and locally sourced materials that reflect the city's cultural heritage.
The station facade features wheels of the Konark Temple. Shikhar draws inspiration from Jaganath Temple Puri. The facade showcases Saura paintings of the Saura tribals, adding a unique cultural touch.
Designed for next 50 years, the station will handle 50,000 passengers per day. Station building on both sides will be connected with 18 meter wide Roof Plaza. Circulating area will be improved.
Railways will improve waiting hall and construct AC lounge. The station will have 14 lifts, six escalators, 20 access control gates, three foot over bridges connecting all platforms, spacious parking of more than 7000 square metres, 133 KW solar panel and 1000 KLD water recycling plant.
Goods shed will be improved during the redevelopment of the station. The project will be completed in 30 months, said the official sources from the Railways.

Text1: VIJAYWADA: The finance department's nod is awaited for augmenting the numerical strength of police personnel in Andhra Pradesh, said director general of police JV Ramudu.
 Addressing senior police officials at a meeting here on Monday, he pointed out that they are looking forward to move the Greyhounds, Octopus training centre, AP Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) and AP Police Academy (APPA) from Hyderabad to the capital region.
 "It is a big challenge for us in developing infrastructure, purchase of equipment and arrangement of sufficient staff in the new state. Proposals have been sent to the chief minister and finance department to arrange funds and land so that we can set up APPA, FSL, Greyhounds and Octopus training centres in the new capital," Ramudu recounted.
 He observed that filling up vacancies for augmentation of force at field level and training the force will be a herculean task with many departments still remaining undivided. The DGP felt that the overall law and order situation in the state is peaceful.
 "In the last 12 months, we dealt with major events such as Godavari Pushkarams, Amaravati foundation ceremony, CII summit and international fleet review in Visakhapatnam. Despite this, effective checks were kept on violence between political parties, communal organisations, activities of Maoists and other anti-social elements," he said.
 Speaking about the plan of action for Krishna Pushkarams, he cited the measures being taken by the department. "Around 33,000 police personnel will be part of the elaborate bandobast. A request has been made to Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and the Union home ministry for allotment of disaster rescue force," the DGP recounted while highlighting the need for parking arrangements, 'May I Help U' booths, iron mesh barricade at ghats, watchtowers, quick reaction teams, pickets and outposts and anti-sabotage check teams.
 He said that all CCTV cameras installed in pushkar ghats will be linked to a single master control apart from several sub-controls to help dedicated police staff monitor the movement of pilgrims. "With the help of CCTV cameras, police can manage the crowd at the ghats and avoid any untoward incidents," Ramudu emphasised.

Text1: PUNE: In a major blow to Indian tennis, the  ATP 250  men's tennis event that had been held in India for the past 27 years has been moved to Hong Kong.
The tournament, which was first held in 1996 in New Delhi, had been conducted in Pune since 2018 under the banner  Tata Open Maharashtra . Chennai had been its home for 21 years in between.
The five-year deal between  IMG , the rights holder for the tournament in the first week of the  ATP calendar , and the Maharashtra government and the state tennis association ( MSLTA ) expired with the completion of the 2023 edition.
It is understood that IMG's demands were unviable for the host - a million dollars (Rs. 8.3 crore approximately for hosting rights, as against the existing fee of Rs 3.5 crore), $700,000 (Rs. 5.8 crore) towards prize money, besides bearing the operating costs, which could be Rs. 5 crore. On top of it, the television, digital and other commercial rights would rest with IMG.
IMG did not respond to a request for comment immediately.
Needless to say, the idea was a non-starter for MSLTA and the Maharashtra government.

"We feel very sad. We did the tournament for five years and the tournament benefited the Indian players.  Rohan Bopanna ,  Ramkumar  and  Divij Sharan  won (the doubles titles) here. Pune was gearing up (to host the event again)," said Prashant Sutar, MSLTA chairman.
Bopanna won the doubles title with Sharan in 2019 and with Ramkumar in 2022. He had also won with Jeevan Nedunchezhiyan when the event was last held in Chennai in 2017.
Somdev Devvarman  reached the final in Chennai, upsetting Carlos Moya on the way, in 2009.
The tournament had attracted the global stars of the game as well - beginning with Tim Henman and Jonas Bjorkman in the inaugural edition in Delhi; Boris Becker, Patrick Rafter, Carlos Moya, Stan Wawrinka, Marin Cilic as well as the legendary Rafael Nadal.
Tamil Nadu Tennis Association, which will also see the WTA Chennai Open taken out of its hand - thanks to tennis returning to China, also expressed disappointment as India was the only stop on the ATP Tour.
"It is unfortunate, a lovely event leaving the country," said Hiten Joshi, CEO of TNTA.
"Unfortunately, the decision is dictated by market forces. How much money can one coff up? It is simply not practical.
"There has to be more equitable distribution of tournaments across the world," he added.
Sunil Yajaman, honorary joint secretary of KSLTA, one of the handful state associations that has been actively hosting tournaments including the Bengaluru Open Challenger, said losing the ATP event was "a big blow to Indian sports, not just tennis" in the country.
"It is certainly disappointing. Any good tennis country needs to have a flagship event, around which there can be Challengers and other smaller tournaments," Yajaman said. 
He believed the country needs to host a Tour event irrespective of whether an Indian was ranked in the top-300 in the world.

Text2: This weekend's refugee drowning crisis in the Mediterranean throws into shameful relief the parochialism of Britain's 2015 general election campaign. It is not just about immigration versus humanitarianism, a topic which attracts glib sentiments from both sides. Nor is it just about us. Right across the EU, leaders and the led seem to focus their attention on ever-narrower horizons. It will do none of us much good. "Stop the world, I want to get off" rarely works for long because the pressures of the world have always managed to force their way in during the whole of recorded history. It has never been more easily done than in today's interconnected world of satellite TV and cheap air travel, especially when national and global institutions capable of imposing some order – they range from the UN to the US, the EU to the IMF – have become so enfeebled. EU divisions will again be on display on Monday. We ought to be talking about this sort of danger in the election campaign, certainly in those televised leaders' debates many of us watched. Immigration and refugees? Interventionism in foreign conflicts, where staying out has been about as successful in Syria as intervening was in Libya? Foreign aid – not to forget the linchpin policy, UK membership of the EU or the imperatives of climate change? All are treated not as strategic issues for our times, but as mere tactics, sticks with which to beat an opponent. By the standards of even the recent past triple-election-winners such as Margaret Thatcher and Tony Blair, whose moral populism extended well beyond these shores, the major party leaders in 2015 are unimpressive enough. When did Dave, Ed or Nick last make a weighty campaign speech on foreign policy? Labour's Douglas Alexander tried, but has Phil Hammond ("The worst foreign secretary in history," an unkind Tory tells me) had a go? I must have missed it in the flurry of unfunded, ill-planned Osborne bribes to voters who know the country can't afford most of them and probably won't. But the minor parties, which might be expected to offer more innovative alternatives (and do so in several modest ways), are even worse. Yes, I know the Greens have a big-picture view of things.
